name: Andy Warhol
hook: Soup cans, silkscreens, and fifteen minutes: the Pop artist whose factory made fame a subject.

facts.label: Pop Art
facts.statement: Andy Warhol and Roy Lichtenstein were leading figures of Pop Art, the movement that turned commercial imagery into fine art.

facts.label: Campbell's Soup Cans
facts.statement: Warhol's Campbell's Soup Cans made the grocery shelf into art; a book on the Campbell Soup Company reproduces 12 pages of his work.

facts.label: fifteen minutes of fame
facts.statement: Warhol said that in the future everyone will be world-famous for 15 minutes.

facts.label: Valerie Solanas
facts.statement: In 1968 Valerie Solanas shot Warhol; months later she wrote to him, "I'm very happy you're alive + well."

facts.label: Interview magazine
facts.statement: Warhol founded Interview magazine in 1969; it was nicknamed the "Crystal Ball of Pop."

facts.label: silkscreen printing
facts.statement: Warhol made many of his pictures by silkscreen, also called serigraphy, a stencil process that let him repeat images mechanically.

facts.label: the Velvet Underground
facts.statement: Warhol managed the Velvet Underground from 1965 and produced their first album, whose cover is his famous banana.
